intro: Pioneer is a private vocational training center, registered by the Ministry of Education and Sports (PSS/P/34), with UBTEB examination centers for Technical and Business (UBT125 and UBB093 respectively), and MAC127 for the Directorate of Industrial Training (MOES). Pioneer is a member of UGAPRIV.
why: The institute addresses the plight of unemployment and underemployment problems which are rampant in the country. Pioneer provides broad competence-based education and training, stimulating the talents of every trainee for further horizontal and vertical mobility in education and training. It prepares trainees for both formal and informal employment (self-employment) — the institute's motto, Self Reliance, lays out the aim of the training at the center.
target_group: All youth above 14 years of age, male and female, regardless of academic background — school leavers and technical affiliates from industries and organisations. The disabled and others with special needs are all welcome.
training: Training includes skills, production and entrepreneurship, stressing 75% hands-on job learning and 25% theory. All courses offered have production units which offer services and products to the public for hire or purchase — trainees participate under instructors' supervision and also train in customer care. It is mandatory for trainees, after a minimum of 9 months (or depending on ability), to be attached to industries or a place of work for exposure to more practical work in line with their training.
accreditation: Training follows two curricula: one from the Directorate of Industrial Training (DIT) for competence, and the other from UBTEB — both under the Ministry of Education and Sports. On completion of a course, trainees sit for Trade Test Exams (skills/practical competence-based) of DIT and UBTEB, and a successful trainee receives two certificates plus a testimonial from the industry/organisation where they had industrial training.
